# The viewer on Qollab {#sec-viewer-qollab}

This page explains how the viewer of `frontend/index.html` runs on Qollab, and how
to change it without breaking that. Read it before changing the viewer, the
measurement, `qollab_api.py` or `scripts/package_qollab.py`.

## The rule {.unnumbered}

**The look and the functions of the viewer are not changed without approval of
the team.** The viewer is a standalone page: it works without Qollab, served by
`python -m http.server`, and it must keep doing so. Everything that Qollab needs
is added as an optional hook (see below) or is generated at build time. A change
that alters what the viewer shows, or how it behaves when it is used alone, has
to be agreed first.

## What Qollab does and does not allow {.unnumbered}

These facts come from the documentation of Qollab (`documentation/prompts/
qollab_context.md`), and they decide the design.

| Fact | Consequence |
| --- | --- |
| The project type is decided by the files of the root: `index.html` and `main.js` make a JS project. | The project that is uploaded needs `index.html` and `main.js` in its root. |
| `index.html` is body content only, and its `<script>` tags do not run. | The script of the viewer goes to `main.js`. |
| Only `main.css` is loaded as a style sheet. | The style of the viewer goes to `main.css`. |
| JS cannot read the files of the project. | The shaders and the laser model are embedded in `main.js`, and the circuits come from Python, not from `out/`. |
| Python is called from JS with `callPromising`, and a `dict` arrives as a `Map`. | `qollab_api.py` returns text (JSON strings). |
| `three` (0.186.1) is imported by name, and the import map of the viewer is not read. | The prelude imports `three` and the addons, and the `import` lines of the viewer are removed. |
| At most 100 files per project, 2 MB each. | The repository (more than 100 files) is not uploaded as it is. |
| IonQ backends accept one job per run. | Only the first compilation works on IonQ. Measuring sends no job. |
| A JS project runs in a sandboxed iframe. | The viewer has its own `body`, so its CSS is copied as it is. |

## How it is built {.unnumbered}

```bash
make qollab
```

The command runs `scripts/package_qollab.py`, which writes the folder `qollab/`
(not committed). Its **content** is uploaded to Qollab. The folder has:

| File | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `index.html` | The markup of the `<body>` of `frontend/index.html`, without the script. |
| `main.css` | The `<style>` block of `frontend/index.html`, unchanged. |
| `main.js` | A generated prelude (the Qollab services), then all the modules of `frontend/js` bundled in one script. |
| `qollab_api.py`, `requirements.txt` | The files of the root. |
| `backend/`, `examples/` | The libraries. |

`main.py` is left out on purpose. In a JS project it could also run, compile a
second time and spend a second IonQ job. The viewer does what `main.py` does.

The viewer is copied, not rewritten, so a change in `frontend/index.html` or in
`frontend/js` reaches Qollab with `make qollab` and nothing else. Do not edit the files of `qollab/`.

## The prelude of `main.js` {.unnumbered}

The viewer is modular (`frontend/js`), but Qollab serves no file of the project
besides the ones it loads itself: a relative `import("./js/main.js")` fails there
with `TypeError: error loading dynamically imported module: …/_nuxt/js/main.js`.
So `main.js` is **one script**: the prelude, followed by the modules bundled by
`bundle_modules` in `scripts/package_qollab.py`. The prelude runs first, so that
the host is ready when the modules read it.

1. **The host.** It defines `window.QVIZ_HOST` with the services below. If
   Python cannot be reached, the message is shown in the `error` line of the
   viewer, and the viewer falls back to its own behavior.
   When Python raises an error of QViz (for example, a machine that is not
   supported), the prelude keeps only its message and drops the traceback, so
   the `error` line shows a sentence a person can read. Any other error is shown
   as it is.
2. **The files.** `shaders/` (`bloch` and `lens`) and `models/laser_lens.obj` and
   `.mtl` are embedded as strings, because the viewer cannot `fetch` them.
3. **The modules.** Each module of `frontend/js` becomes an `async` function with
   its own scope, in the order of their imports, and returns what it exports; the
   modules that import it destructure that object. Two modules may therefore
   declare the same private name. The imports of `three` are kept once at the
   top. The addons are loaded in `three-addons.js` with a fallback, so that the
   viewer starts without the laser and the environment light when an addon is not
   available. The bundler follows the style of the modules: `export` before a
   declaration, `import {…}` or `import * as x` from `./name.js`; `export
   default`, `export { … }` and default imports are rejected at build time.

## The hooks of the viewer {.unnumbered}

The viewer reads `window.QVIZ_HOST` once, as `HOST`. Every field is optional. When
a field is missing, the viewer does what it always did.

| Field | Type | What the viewer does with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shaders` | `{vert, frag, lensVert, lensFrag}` | Uses these sources, instead of fetching `shaders/`. |
| `laser` | `{obj, mtl}` | Parses this text for the laser model, instead of fetching `models/`. |
| `circuits` | `[{file, label}]` | Lists them in the selector, instead of reading `out/manifest.json`. |
| `load` | `async (file) -> object` | Gets the JSON of an entry of the selector, instead of fetching `out/<file>`. |
| `sample` | `async (data, step, shots) -> [[bitstring, count], …]` | Measures with the backend. |
| `compileQasm` | `async (text) -> object` | Compiles a circuit written in OpenQASM 2 or 3 (`qollab_api.run_qasm`, without the IonQ job). It is how the user loads a circuit: the button *Cargar circuito* and dropping a `.qasm` file both call it, and the circuit becomes a new entry of the selector. The viewer no longer loads JSON files; without this hook it asks the local server (`make server`). |

The test `test_every_service_of_the_prelude_is_used_by_the_viewer` fails if the
prelude defines a service that the viewer does not read. **To add a service:**
read it in `frontend/index.html` as `HOST.<name>` with a fallback for when it is
missing, define it in the prelude of `scripts/package_qollab.py`, add the Python
function to `qollab_api.py` if it needs one, and document it in this table.

## The measurement {.unnumbered}

The `Medir` button always draws the outcomes with the backend: `HOST.sample` on
Qollab, or `POST /api/sample` of the local server (`make server`), which runs the
same function.

1. `HOST.sample(data, step, shots)` sends the JSON text of the current file, the
   step and the shots to `qollab_api.sample_step`, which calls `backend.sample`
   (see the [sampler](../modules/sampler.qmd)).
2. The reply is a list of `[bitstring, count]` pairs, from the most to the least
   frequent. It is a list and not an object because JavaScript sorts the
   integer-like keys of an object (`"10"`, `"11"`).
3. The panel is drawn as before, without the note about entanglement, because the
   measurement keeps the correlations.
4. If the backend fails, or there is no Python, the error is shown. There is no
   fallback: sampling the marginals independently does not model entanglement.
5. If the user changes the step or the file while Python works, the reply is
   dropped.

On Qollab, a Bell pair at its last step gives `00` and `11` only, and at step 4
it gives `01` and `10` at about 50 % each.

## `qollab_api.py` {.unnumbered}

Each function is called from JS with `callPromising`, and takes and returns plain
values or text.

| Function | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `circuits()` | The example circuits, as JSON text: `[{"file", "label"}]`. |
| `run(backend, circuit, shots, entangler)` | Compiles an example circuit and returns the JSON text. |
| `run_qasm(backend, qasm, shots, entangler)` | Compiles a circuit written in OpenQASM 2 or 3, locally (no IonQ job), and returns the JSON text. |
| `sample_step(visualization, step, shots)` | Measures a step and returns the counts as a JSON list of pairs. |

## How it was verified {.unnumbered}

On Qollab (Built-in simulator, qiskit 2.5.2, qiskit-ionq 1.0.2, NumPy 2.4.6, with
Pyodide v314.0.7) a diagnostic page (since removed; it is in the git history) passed all the checks: the call from a
click works after the first run, and compilation of a Bell pair and each
measurement took a few milliseconds.

Locally, the generated `main.js` was run with the real Python and a simulated
page (jsdom, with no WebGL), and the measurement panel gave the expected results
with the backend, without a sampler in the host, and when the backend fails.

**Not verified yet** (it needs Qollab): that `three/addons/` resolves there, the 3D
scene with the newer three.js (shaders, labels, laser, lens and colors), the size
of the viewer inside the iframe, and the behavior on the IonQ simulators. Compare
the scene with the standalone viewer.

## Rules for future changes {.unnumbered}

- Do not change how the viewer looks or what it does without approval. A change
  for Qollab goes in a hook or in the prelude, not in the viewer.
- Keep the viewer working alone: with `HOST` empty, it must behave as before.
- Python functions that JS calls return text, never a `dict`, and ordered data is
  returned as a list.
- Do not call `backend.run` from a function that a click calls. On IonQ it is one
  job per run.
- After a change, run `make test`, then `make qollab`, upload the folder and run
  the diagnostic page if anything fails.
- Keep `requirements.txt` equal to `pyproject.toml`, and inside the versions of
  [the installation page](../getting-started/installation.qmd).
